reasoning: Both sets come from the same planning pipeline and share the same skeleton: a single rllab package, interface-first M1 with spines, wiring, thicken and system phases, frozen contracts and per-task context packets. They differ in RL depth, milestone shape and packet completeness. B teaches RL better. Snake has a tabular → DQN → full-grid CNN ladder with memory, target-copy and exploration ablations, and a corridor proves the core. The fish tank runs REINFORCE vs PPO as a tested claim, and predator-prey moves from fixed opponents to naive co-learning to pool self-play, with cross-play tables and ratings. B separates truncation from termination explicitly for bootstrapping, and its closed-form golden cases are correct (Q-update 0.1/0.009, GAE 1.3775/0.5, the clipped objective, ball and catch geometry). A is sound but thinner: online-Q and REINFORCE spines that later grow into DQN and PPO, a check-world gate and a paired permutation test with Holm correction. A's strengths are a learner write-up feature that serves the user's 'explain why it works' goal and finer milestones: the fish tank is split one fish / many fish / local sight along real dependency lines. But A's M1 doesn't deliver a watchable replay. M3 ('Check and explain the snake') is a leftover carve-off of reference check plus write-up. A's interface task freezes private thicken hooks (guard, check_runs, apply_style, holm, verdict), and its tests.md still has unresolved fallout from the fish-score change (TC-07). B's packets are more self-contained. Its M1-T06 spine packet carries every type the loop touches, while A's M1-T09 and M1-T17 packets leave out core.Step, WorldSpec and EpisodeResult and the stub signatures they must call. B has its own consistency problems. Its brief says 'Not doing: designing future environments now' while the spec and AD-09/AD-13 design all three up front, and CORE-06 and the roadmap still speak of a later 'interface revision'. B's milestones are also coarse: one per stage, so M1 is the whole stage rather than a walking skeleton. Overall B's stronger RL content and better buildability narrowly beat A's finer milestones and plainer prose.

strengths: Plain-language spec with concrete Given/When/Then for every requirement
Learner write-up feature (NOTES) and finish check directly serve 'explain why it works'
Fish tank split into one / many / local-sight milestones along real dependency lines, each with checkable Exit
Rigorous evaluation: disjoint seed ranges, paired permutation test, Holm correction, every-run-beats-rule verdict, collapse flag
Clear 12-pipeline step tables with entry sketches; component-per-folder layout
weaknesses: M1 delivers no replay, so the user can't watch the trained snake until M2
M3 'Check and explain the snake' is a leftover milestone of reference check plus write-up
Interface task freezes private thicken hooks (guard, check_runs, apply_style, holm, verdict) as stubs
Stale or unresolved test text after the fish-score change (TC-07) and routes still pending
Several spine packets leave out types they need (core.Step, WorldSpec, EpisodeResult, stub signatures)

strengths: Strong RL pedagogy: value ladder with ablations, REINFORCE vs PPO comparison, naive co-learning vs opponent-pool self-play with cross-play and ratings
Truncation/termination separation and batch-first multi-team core designed up front to serve all three stages
Closed-form golden cases cite sources (Sutton & Barto, Schulman et al.) and are arithmetically correct
Library-reference mapping pinned parameter by parameter (AD-04, AD-10, AD-11) so a REF-02 gap points at the learner's code
Context packets are largely self-contained, carrying every type a spine touches
weaknesses: Brief contradicts the plan ('Not doing: designing future environments now'; success criteria only mention Snake)
CORE-06 and the roadmap S2 outline describe a later 'interface revision' that AD-09 moved before M1
One milestone per stage, so M1 is the whole stage rather than a walking skeleton
PL-01 step table mixes 16 alternative implementations as 'steps'; PL-04 entry sketch uses curves.ladder/.ablations, which its step table doesn't produce
No write-up artifact for 'explain in my own words'
